summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics (induction, sets, modular arithmetic, primes, permutations, binary representation), algorithm analysis with recurrences, and a first course in linear algebra (vector spaces, subspaces, dimension, invertible and triangular matrices). They know big-O, polynomials, complex numbers including roots of unity, and basic Turing machines with tapes. They have not studied the FFT-based multiplication literature, Schönhage–Strassen, Nussbaumer transforms, multitape complexity theory in depth, or numerical error analysis beyond basics.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: Arithmetic on remainders modulo an integer, with a ≡ b (mod m) meaning m divides a−b.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: Primes are integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors, and two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

known.name: Binary representation and bit operations
known.gloss: Nonnegative integers written in base 2 as bit strings, with bitwise exclusive-or as addition of bits modulo 2.

known.name: Floors, ceilings and logarithms
known.gloss: Rounding down or up to an integer and the base-2 logarithm, with lg n the number of bits needed for n.

known.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: Θ and Ω express tight and lower asymptotic bounds on growth, as O expresses upper bounds.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
known.gloss: Sets closed under linear combinations, described by spanning sets and bases, with dimension the size of a basis.

known.name: Matrices, invertibility and linear maps
known.gloss: Matrices represent linear maps; invertible ones can be undone, and products of matrices compose maps.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite set onto itself, used to rearrange the order of array entries.

known.name: Cartesian products and index tuples
known.gloss: The set of tuples with each entry from its own set, indexing multidimensional arrays.

known.name: Mathematical induction and recurrences
known.gloss: Proving statements for all sizes by a base case and a step, and solving cost recurrences of recursive algorithms.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and linear-time addition
known.gloss: Adding n-bit integers takes linear time, and the long-multiplication method takes quadratic time.

known.name: Cyclic and negacyclic indexing
known.gloss: Indices taken modulo N so that positions wrap around, forming the cyclic group of integers modulo N.

known.name: Dyadic rationals and fixed-point numbers
known.gloss: Numbers of the form integer over a power of two, stored as an integer with an implied binary point.

known.name: Sup norm and rounding error bounds
known.gloss: The maximum absolute value of the entries of a vector, used to bound errors so that rounding recovers an integer.

known.name: Real and imaginary parts, complex conjugate and modulus
aliases: absolute value of a complex number
known.gloss: Decomposing a complex number a+bi into components, with modulus sqrt(a²+b²); Gaussian integers have integer a and b.

known.name: Summation, geometric series and inequalities
known.gloss: Manipulating finite sums and bounding them with standard inequalities.
